draft.title: Water's beauty and spiritual meaning
card: People value water for its beauty. Waterfalls, bays and lakes are places many people enjoy looking at and visiting.
Some beautiful water places are protected as national parks or World Heritage sites. Protection helps keep them in good condition for the future.
People also value water for its spiritual meaning. Many faiths and cultures treat certain waters as holy.
The Ganges River in India is sacred to Hindus. Many Hindus bathe in it or hold ceremonies on its banks.
draft.remember: People value water for its beauty and for its spiritual meaning, and some water places are protected for these reasons.

a.q: Why do many Hindus value the Ganges River?
opts: It is sacred, so they hold ceremonies and bathe in it
It is the largest river that is used for irrigated rice
It is a bay that is protected as a national park
It is a waterfall that attracts tourists each year
a.why: The Ganges holds spiritual meaning for Hindus, who bathe in it and hold ceremonies there. Irrigation, parks and waterfalls are other ways of valuing water, but they are not why Hindus honour the Ganges.
a.clue: Think of the spiritual meaning of the river.

b.q: A bay is protected as a World Heritage site because people value its scenery. Which value of water does this show?
opts: Its beauty
Its use in irrigation
Its use in town supply
Its role as a border
b.why: The bay is protected because people value how it looks, which is its beauty. Irrigation and town supply are economic uses, and a border is a different idea.
b.clue: The bay is protected for how it looks.

a.best: It is sacred, so they hold ceremonies and bathe in it

problems.detail: The remember line says water places are protected for both beauty and spiritual meaning, but the card only says beautiful water places are protected. It says more than the card teaches.

The stem says people value the bay's scenery, and the clue says it is protected for how it looks. Together they all but state the answer 'beauty', so a student can match the synonym without knowing the idea.

The distractors call the Ganges a bay or a waterfall, which are clearly wrong. Only the right option mentions anything spiritual, so the question is very easy even without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Water's beauty and spiritual meaning
card: People value water for more than drinking or farming. Many value it for its beauty, such as waterfalls, bays and lakes they enjoy seeing and visiting.
Some beautiful water places are protected as national parks or World Heritage sites. Protection helps keep them in good condition for the future.
People can also value water for its spiritual meaning. Many faiths and cultures treat certain waters as holy, or sacred.
The Ganges River in India is sacred to Hindus. Many Hindus bathe in it or hold ceremonies on its banks as part of their faith.
proposal.remember: Water can matter to people for how it looks and for what it means to their faith.

a.q: Many Hindus travel to the Ganges River to bathe in it during festivals. Which value of water does this mainly show?
opts: Its spiritual meaning in their faith
Its beauty as a scenic place to visit
Its use as a supply of drinking water
Its use for watering crops on farms
a.why: Hindus bathe in the Ganges because it is sacred in their faith, so this shows its spiritual meaning. Visiting might sound like beauty, but they go for a religious reason, not for the view.
a.clue: Think about why they bathe there, not just that they travel.

b.q: Which of these shows people valuing water mainly for its beauty?
opts: Hikers walk to a lookout to see a waterfall
Pilgrims bathe in a river during a holy festival
A farmer pumps river water onto a rice crop
A town builds a dam to store drinking water
b.why: The hikers go to the waterfall to enjoy how it looks, which is its beauty. The pilgrims are a tempting choice because they also visit water, but they go for its spiritual meaning. The farm and the dam are everyday uses.
b.clue: Think about why each person goes to the water.

a.best: Its spiritual meaning in their faith

b.best: Hikers walk to a lookout to see a waterfall
